cases.prompt: This parser panics on bad input from clients. Make it return errors instead, and add tests.

all.why: defines the error with thiserror, which the crate already uses

expectations: Every slice index on untrusted input is replaced by a length check or `.get(...)`, so short or truncated buffers return an error.
No `unwrap()` or `expect()` is added on the input path.
Tests cover at least an empty buffer and a buffer shorter than its declared length, in a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block or under tests/.

cases.prompt: Clippy warns about this, and under load the server sometimes stalls. What is going on?

any.why: explains the guard is held across the await

expectations: Explains that the std::sync::Mutex guard is held across `.await`, which blocks other tasks on that lock and can stall the runtime.
Fixes it by releasing the guard before the await (and re-locking to insert) or by using an async mutex.
Mentions that `lock().unwrap()` panics on a poisoned lock, or otherwise avoids unwrap in this server path.

cases.prompt: I changed the `parser` crate in this workspace. What should I run before opening the PR?

all.why: runs tests with cargo-nextest, which the workspace configures

expectations: Uses `cargo nextest run` rather than plain `cargo test`, because the workspace has a nextest config.
Runs clippy with warnings denied (for example `-- -D warnings`) over all targets.
Scopes a quick run to the parser crate (`-p parser`) and also runs the whole workspace, since server and cli may depend on parser.
